about.title: Sobre o LaPS
about.lead: O Laboratório de Processamento de Sinais (LaPS) integra pesquisadores e estudantes vinculados ao Programa de Pós-Graduação em Engenharia Elétrica (PPGEE), à Faculdade de Engenharia da Computação e Telecomunicações (FCT) e à Faculdade de Engenharia Elétrica e Biomédica (FEEB) da Universidade Federal do Pará (UFPA).
about.bullet1: Análise avançada de sinais bioelétricos, EEG e interfaces cérebro-computador (BCI)
about.bullet2: Sistemas de comunicações 5G/6G, MIMO massivo e propagação em ondas milimétricas
about.bullet3: Processamento de imagens, visão computacional e inteligência artificial profunda
about.mission: Nossa missão é desenvolver ciência de fronteira e tecnologia aplicada com impacto global a partir da Região Amazônica.

members.title: Equipe do LaPS
members.subtitle: Pesquisadores, docentes e discentes que impulsionam a ciência e a inovação tecnológica no laboratório:

bios.ana: Graduada em Engenharia da Computação (UFPA, 2008), Mestre e Doutora em Engenharia Elétrica (UFPA, 2010 e 2017). Atua em reconhecimento de padrões, processamento de imagens e aprendizado de máquina, com foco em identificação de padrões neurais via EEG. É professora adjunta na FEEB/UFPA.
bios.antonio: Mestre (1994) e Doutor em Biofísica pela UFRJ (1997), com pós-doutorado em Neurobiologia pela Duke University (2003-2005). Professor associado na FEEB/UFPA, com pesquisa focada em sinais bioelétricos e sistemas de neuroengenharia.
bios.francisco: Graduado (2002), Mestre (2005) e Doutor em Engenharia Elétrica pela UFPA (2010), com estágio doutoral na Virginia Tech (EUA). Especialista em comunicações digitais, classificação de modulação e sistemas DSL. É professor na FCT/UFPA.
bios.ronaldo: Graduado em Engenharia Elétrica (UFPA, 1995), Mestre e Doutor pela UFSC (1998 e 2003), com pós-doutorado na Polytech Nantes (França, 2016). Professor associado na FCT/UFPA, pesquisa avaliação de qualidade visual, modelos de atenção e eye-tracking.

about.title: About LaPS
about.lead: The Signal Processing Laboratory (LaPS) brings together faculty and graduate students associated with the Graduate Program in Electrical Engineering (PPGEE), the Faculty of Computer and Telecommunications Engineering (FCT), and the Faculty of Electrical and Biomedical Engineering (FEEB) at the Federal University of Pará (UFPA).
about.bullet1: Advanced bioelectric signal analysis, EEG, and brain-computer interfaces (BCI)
about.bullet2: 5G/6G communication systems, massive MIMO, and millimeter-wave propagation
about.bullet3: Image processing, computer vision, and deep artificial intelligence
about.mission: Our mission is to foster cutting-edge science and applied technologies with global impact originating from the Amazon Region.

areas.title: Research Areas
areas.subtitle: Scientific pillars oriented toward foundational theory and high-impact technological applications:

area5g.title: 5G / 6G Communication Systems
area5g.item1: Hybrid beamforming architectures for spatial user multiplexing in massive MIMO
area5g.item2: Deterministic millimeter-wave propagation channel modeling via ray-tracing
area5g.item3: Spectral optimization and energy efficiency in cellular wireless networks

areaBio.title: Bioelectric Signals & Neuroengineering
areaBio.item1: Electrophysiological investigation in neural conditions (epilepsy, autism, ADHD)
areaBio.item2: EEG, EMG, and ECG signal processing using time-frequency decomposition
areaBio.item3: Adaptive neurofeedback systems for cognitive and motor rehabilitation

areaVision.title: Computer Vision & Image Processing
areaVision.item2: Human action recognition and pose estimation via deep learning
areaVision.item3: Eye-tracking systems and visual attention computational models

members.title: LaPS Team
members.subtitle: Faculty, researchers, and students driving scientific advancement and technological innovation:

bios.ana: B.Sc. in Computer Engineering (UFPA, 2008), M.Sc. and Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering (UFPA, 2010 and 2017). Expert in pattern recognition, image processing, and machine learning, with emphasis on neural pattern decoding from EEG. Associate Professor at FEEB/UFPA.
bios.antonio: M.Sc. (1994) and Ph.D. in Biophysics from UFRJ (1997), postdoctoral fellowship in Neurobiology at Duke University (2003-2005). Associate Professor at FEEB/UFPA, focusing on bioelectric signal analysis and neuroengineering.
bios.francisco: B.Sc. (2002), M.Sc. (2005), and Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from UFPA (2010), with doctoral research exchange at Virginia Tech (USA). Specializes in digital communications, modulation classification, and DSL systems. Professor at FCT/UFPA.
bios.ronaldo: B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering (UFPA, 1995), M.Sc. and Ph.D. from UFSC (1998 and 2003), postdoctoral fellowship at Polytech Nantes (France, 2016). Associate Professor at FCT/UFPA, researching visual quality assessment, visual attention models, and eye-tracking.

lines.ana: Image processing, computer vision, and EEG.
lines.antonio: Bioelectric signal analysis, neurofeedback, and neuroengineering.
lines.ronaldo: Image processing, computer vision, and video analytics.

about.title: À Propos du LaPS
about.lead: Le Laboratoire de Traitement du Signal (LaPS) réunit des enseignants-chercheurs et étudiants rattachés au Programme de Troisième Cycle en Génie Électrique (PPGEE), à la Faculté d'Ingénierie Informatique et Télécommunications (FCT) et à la Faculté de Génie Électrique et Biomédical (FEEB) de l'Université Fédérale du Pará (UFPA).
about.bullet1: Analyse avancée de signaux bioélectriques, EEG et interfaces cerveau-machine (BCI)
about.bullet2: Systèmes de communication 5G/6G, MIMO massif et propagation en ondes millimétriques
about.bullet3: Traitement d'images, vision par ordinateur et apprentissage profond
about.mission: Notre mission est de faire progresser la science fondamentale et les technologies appliquées à portée mondiale depuis la région amazonienne.

area5g.item2: Modélisation déterministe du canal de propagation en ondes millimétriques par lancer de rayons
area5g.item3: Optimisation spectrale et efficacité énergétique dans les réseaux sans fil cellulaires

areaBio.item2: Traitement des signaux EEG, EMG et ECG avec décomposition temps-fréquence
areaBio.item3: Systèmes adaptatifs de neurofeedback pour la réhabilitation cognitive et motrice
